Walk through the folders again, with what each one is for.

knotes keeps your notes as ordinary text files on this device — one file per note, named by the moment you wrote it. Nothing is locked in an app database: the same files open on your computer, and a note you delete here is a file that is gone.
The next few screens point the app at the folders it should read. Each one turns on a part of the app, and each says which.
Nothing here is permanent — every answer is in Settings afterwards, and you can reopen this tour from there. Skip setup at any point if you would rather explore first.
The home screen writes and lists notes here. Each note is one Markdown file; when you attach files to a note they go in a companion folder beside it, named after the note.
If you already keep notes in a folder — synced from a computer, say — point this at that folder and they appear immediately. Otherwise the default below is a good place to start.

The Collect page gathers recent screenshots, photos and voice recordings from the folders your other apps write to, and turns the ones you choose into a note with the files attached — so a screenshot becomes something you can title, tag and find again.

resources.string: This is not your notes folder. Collected notes will not appear on the home screen, and the desktop app won\'t read them as notes.

Point this at your audio and video and the app becomes a player built for working through them: it remembers where you stopped in every file, and lets you drop timestamped bookmarks with a note attached to each.

It can also choose what plays next for you — the next file in the folder, a forgotten unbookmarked file from anywhere in the library, or a random one from the folder you\'re in. Files attached to your notes are playable the same way.

resources.string: The Gallery page browses a folder of images and lets you draw on them — arrows, boxes and text burnt into a copy, so a marked-up screenshot can be attached to a note or sent on.

knotes works entirely on its own. If you also run Nibras, connecting it adds your tasks, journal, planner and resources to this app: the records you have bookmarked sync down to the phone, you can read and edit them offline, and anything you change is sent back when the connection returns.
Leave this blank to skip — you can connect later in Settings.
Notes on this phone are never sent to Nibras by this connection — they stay files in your notes folder. This is for the records that already live on the server.
Plans with a time can alert you before they start, and the app can sound a quiet chime on the quarter hour so time passing is noticeable without looking at anything.
Shows today\'s note count, and keeps the app running so reminders and the chime actually fire.
